solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sorrow reduced by singer and actor

indicators.note: reduced means the word for sorrow is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a cross to bear is a sorrow or burden
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grief cuts down a performer famous for both singing and acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims CROSS to CROS. Bing Crosby was an American crooner and film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was a celebrated American crooner who also starred in many films.

clue.text: Spies capturing a married person in the country

indicators.note: capturing means the spies' letters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies
taken as written
bod is informal British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents seize a wedded individual somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is informal British slang for a person, a 'body'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in Southeast Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Trader away from the shop and healthier?

parts.note: someone away from the shop is out
fitter means in better health

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who is out of the store and in better shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of the clothing merchant's name as a phrase about someone out of the shop and in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a merchant who sells clothes and equipment, so a kind of trader.

clue.text: Pope's pronouncement is nonsense

definitions.meaning: a papal ... is an official edict issued by the Pope
..., short for a cruder word, is slang for rubbish talk

explanation.definitionFit: A papal bull is a formal decree, and bull is also slang for empty talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Maybe enlightened editors will bring in university lion?

indicators.note: will bring in means the editors' letters take the other pieces inside

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, so two editors give ED twice
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Editors admitting a lion from a university might be thought wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'editors' supplies the editor abbreviation twice, one either side. 'Maybe' marks enlightened as only one sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An educated person is schooled and informed, one example of being enlightened, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Long bit of land in the river for all

indicators.note: in means the strip of land sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, a crossword favourite
a spit is a long narrow strip of land jutting into water

explanation.surface: A narrow headland sitting in a river, available to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland. 'For all' is used as in 'for all his faults', meaning in spite of.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite and for all both mean notwithstanding, as in for all that or in spite of that.

clue.text: Famous Prussian circus open after reorganisation

indicators.note: after reorganisation means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big-top show opening after being restructured, featuring a celebrated Prussian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reorganisation' rearranges CIRCUSOPEN. Copernicus was born in Royal Prussia, then part of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolaus Copernicus, the astronomer, came from Toruń in Royal Prussia and is world famous.

clue.text: Body slim? Good!

parts.note: slim means thin

explanation.surface: Someone pleased to see a slender figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object or entity, and a body can likewise mean any physical object.

clue.text: Mild objection gets epic picture banned

parts.note: a demur is a raised objection

indicators.note: banned means the picture's letters are excluded from the word epic

parts.note: pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A gentle protest results in a grand film being prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned' removes PIC from EPIC, leaving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure means modest and reserved, close to mild in manner.

clue.text: Author providing grim end to tale

parts.note: grim means stern

indicators.note: end to picks the final letter of the word tale

explanation.surface: A writer supplies a bleak ending to a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist, so he is an author.

clue.text: Meat is ultimately in short supply, upsetting butchers

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in short supply means the word ultimately is heavily cut down to its abbreviated form

explanation.surface: Meat is ultimately scarce, which troubles those who sell it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' cuts ULTIMATELY to ULT (as in the abbreviation ult.); 'upsetting' rearranges MEATIS plus ULT. The butchers of the surface are a noun; the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to hack about savagely, which is what mutilating means.

clue.text: King, one sitting in a small carriage

indicators.note: sitting in means the letter for one is placed inside the carriage

parts.note: a pram is a small carriage for a baby
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monarch, a lone figure, perched inside a little vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the ruler of Troy during the Trojan War in Greek myth.

clue.text: Start with olive oil being put around dish

indicators.note: Start with picks the first letter of the word olive
being put around means the word oil is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: begin with olive oil and coat a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put around' looks like it wants one piece wrapped round another, but here it means turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy stew of mixed meats and vegetables, a dish of Spanish origin.

clue.text: Dealer in a right scrap, one demonstrating anger

parts.note: taken as written
a scrap is a bit
someone who rages is a rager

explanation.surface: A trader caught up in a proper fight, furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but means a small bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrager trades to profit from price differences between markets, so a financial dealer.

clue.text: Provoke the hostility of one against change

indicators.note: change means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stirring up a person who opposes reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges ONEAGAINST.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to make them hostile, which is to provoke their hostility.

clue.text: In future perhaps will be passionate

parts.note: taken as written
the future is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone predicting that ardour lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'future perhaps' is a grammatical tense, not time ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and fervent, much the same as passionate ones.

clue.text: Time to restrict greedy person, one of an undistinguished generation?

indicators.note: to restrict means the time word encloses the greedy person

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time
a pig is slang for a greedy person

explanation.surface: Curbing a glutton over time, perhaps a mediocre successor.
explanation.walkthrough: An epigon (or epigone) is a lesser imitator following a great predecessor; the question mark admits the definition is descriptive.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigon is an imitative follower of a great artist, typically one of a lesser later generation.

clue.text: Spontaneously throbbing after love game

indicators.note: after means the throbbing piece follows love and game

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
nim is a game of taking matchsticks or counters
a pulse is a throbbing beat

explanation.surface: Acting on a whim, heart racing after a romantic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: NIM is a game in which players take turns removing objects from piles.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on impulse means doing it suddenly without planning, spontaneously.

clue.text: Guard parking at front of national park

indicators.note: at front of means the parking letter is placed before the park

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a nature reserve is a protected area like a national park

explanation.surface: Protect the parking area at the entrance to a national park.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to protect and keep it safe, which is to guard it.

clue.text: Start to talk about ornament in the auditorium

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so the word is a soundalike

parts.note: a brooch is a decorative pin or ornament

explanation.surface: A speaker begins to discuss a piece of jewellery in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOCH and BROACH sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion for the first time.

clue.text: Stew that's very warm, a food not entirely eaten

indicators.note: eaten means the inner pieces are swallowed up by the word for very warm

parts.note: hot means very warm
taken as written

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the food is dropped

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A hot stew, with some of the food left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' looks like part of the food picture but is the container signal: the very warm word swallows A and the shortened food.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot, or haricot mutton, is a traditional stew of mutton with vegetables.

clue.text: Messenger, one proclaiming the news outside Oxford University

indicators.note: outside means the town crier's letters wrap around the university

parts.note: a town crier publicly announces news

explanation.surface: A town crier announcing news beyond the Oxford college gates.
explanation.walkthrough: A town crier was an official who called out public announcements in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries messages or packages, making them a messenger.

clue.text: Relation making money across America

indicators.note: across means the money word spans the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A relative earns cash across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' signals that the money word spans America, enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle, so a relation.

clue.text: Endless fish served up and a slice of meat

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the trimmed fish is read from bottom to top
Endless means the final letter of the fish is dropped

parts.note: a pollock is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Fish served with a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts POLLOCK to POLLOC; 'served up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A collop is an old word for a thin slice or escalope of meat.

clue.text: Work for head of institute in Birmingham brings disgrace

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: in means the institute's first letter sits inside the city's nickname

parts.note: Brum is the British nickname for the city of Birmingham

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word institute

explanation.surface: Working for the head of an institute in Birmingham brings shame.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the everyday British nickname for Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public disgrace or harsh criticism that brings shame.

clue.text: Girl that's acceptable when thoughts are out in the open?

definitions.text: that's acceptable when thoughts are out in the open
definitions.meaning: the coin offered in the saying about paying for someone's thoughts

explanation.walkthrough: 'A penny for your thoughts' asks someone to share what they are thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny is a girl's name, and a penny is the coin in the idiom offering payment for thoughts.

clue.text: Fruit in orchard — no place for animals

indicators.note: no means the place abbreviation is taken out of the fruit

parts.note: apples are fruit grown in an orchard

explanation.surface: Fruit in an orchard where animals do not belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes PL from APPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes are primates such as gorillas and chimpanzees, so animals.

clue.text: Animal with hair deprived of tail

indicators.note: deprived of tail means the final letter of the hair word is cut off

parts.note: a beard is facial hair

explanation.surface: A furry creature that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of tail' cuts BEARD to BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear is a large furry mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Porch dreadful — a nail holds it together

indicators.note: holds it together means the run of words contains the answer within it, letters joined across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A shoddy veranda, held together by a single nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' looks like an anagram signal (and A NAIL does rearrange to the answer), but the porch is simply held inside 'dreadful a nail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanai is a Hawaiian veranda or roofed porch.

clue.text: Greek character, trader who cheats people?

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a seller is a trader

explanation.surface: A Greek merchant who swindles customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'one who cheats people'; the question mark admits the trader may not cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller is slang for a swindler, someone who defrauds others.

clue.text: Unknown chaps among dabs getting fees?

indicators.note: among means the other pieces sit inside the word for dabs

parts.note: pats are light dabs
Y is an algebraic unknown
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Anonymous fellows mixing with fingerprint experts get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dabs' suggests fingerprints or flatfish, but here it means light touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments are sums paid out, and fees are payments for services.

clue.text: Suddenly stop releases being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to release is to free, so releases is frees

explanation.surface: Lets go of someone, then abruptly halts at the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: FREES and FREEZE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop moving suddenly and stay still.
